title: Migration plan for embedding normalization and metric correctness
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our embeddings endpoints currently have ambiguous handling for vector norms and distance computation. Some models and SDKs expect dot-product semantics while others assume cosine similarity; historically clients normalized vectors at the SDK or downstream, so server-side behavior drifted. This causes subtle ranking regressions and unpredictable cost/latency profiles when we switch quantized or fp16 kernels.

Goal: Provide a clear, backwards-compatible API for distance metrics, converge on a server-side canonical behavior (L2-normalized vectors + cosine similarity by default), and provide migration tooling and a deprecation path for dot-product-first consumers. Improve correctness for reranking endpoints, reduce client-side code fragmentation, and add tests/benchmarks that detect metric regressions.

Scope: API semantics, embeddings ingestion/return contract, SDK flags, storage of norm metadata, reranker scoring code, query-time normalization options, documentation, and migration guides. Does NOT include upstream model retraining or changes to pretrained model exports.

Proposed solution summary: 1) Default API behavior: embeddings endpoints will return raw vectors plus an optional precomputed_norm field and a metric field set to "cosine". The server will document that the default ranking semantics are cosine similarity on L2-normalized vectors. 2) Backward compatibility: Keep an API query parameter and SDK option (metric=dot|cosine, normalize=true|false) to preserve old behaviors. Provide a server-side compatibility mode that, when enabled by customer, preserves legacy dot-product semantics and stores a versioned flag in the response (api_embedding_schema=v1 for legacy, v2 for normalized). 3) Ingestion/storage: When storing vectors in our internal caches or indexes, persist a compact norm (float32) alongside the vector if the model/client does not supply an explicit normalized vector. This avoids repeated L2 pass at query time for cached items while keeping memory overhead ~4 bytes per vector. 4) Query-time performance: Implement an accelerated L2 normalization kernel in the runtime (batch-normalize on GPU when possible) and fall back to CPU SIMD path for small batches. Add heuristic: if cached norm exists, use precomputed; otherwise normalize on the GPU via continuous batching. 5) Tests & CI: Add unit tests that assert numerical equivalence for normalized-dot -> cosine, end-to-end rerank tests with known datasets (MS MARCO small subset), and a regression monitor over Collector traces. 6) Telemetry: Emit metric "embeddings.metric_used" with values {cosine,dot,legacy} and percentiles for time_spent_normalizing and added_latency_ms.

Rollout plan: alpha behind feature-flag for internal customers -> beta opt-in for existing customers with compatibility flag -> gradual default switch for new API keys after 60 days of notice -> deprecate legacy metric parameter 6 months after default switch.

Migration perks for customers: Provide an "auto-migrate" tool that converts stored legacy vectors to normalized representations offline (GPU batch job) and a verification report that shows ranking deltas for a sample of queries.
acceptance_criteria: API returns explicit metric and optional precomputed_norm field for embeddings responses
SDKs expose metric and normalize flags and default to server-recommended behavior
Server-side storage persists a 32-bit norm when input vectors are not normalized
Reranker tests show no >1% top-5 ranking drift for accounts that enable compatibility mode
Telemetry emits embeddings.metric_used and normalization latency metrics
Performance: 95th percentile added latency from normalization < 5ms for hosted workloads in production profile

notes: Trade-offs: Normalizing at ingestion reduces query-time cost but requires an expensive one-time rewrite. Normalizing at query-time is simpler but increases tail latency for cold cached vectors.
Accuracy vs memory: Storing float32 norm is safest; uint16 quantization may be considered for indexes >1B vectors with explicit error budgets.
Compatibility: Exposing metric param keeps existing workflows intact. We avoid forcing a silent behavior change which historically caused customer regressions.

Benchmarks planned: run A/B on p4d vs a100 for batches of sizes 1, 8, 32; measure added latency and GPU utilization. Also test combined effect of quantized kernels (int8) on cosine distance numeric stability.
